processing: Black tea made along normal Darjeeling lines: withered, rolled, oxidised and dried. No specific smoking step is documented, despite the smoky note drinkers mention.
harvest_season: As across Darjeeling, spring, early-summer and autumn pickings.
appearance_dry: Typical of Darjeeling black tea: dark wiry leaf with some lighter pieces.
appearance_liquor: Amber to copper, typical of Darjeeling black tea from later pickings.
appearance_wet: Coppery brown leaf with some green, as usual for the class.
taste_profile: Known among Indian tea lovers for its aroma and a smoky edge; beyond that, little detail is documented.

brewing.notes: Western style. A good one to try plain first, then with a splash of milk if you prefer it softer.

vintage_note: Sold as a garden brand with a following in India and abroad, much of it exported to Europe. How it is dated varies by seller, so check for a flush, harvest year or packing date. As with other Darjeeling black teas, fresher tea keeps more aroma.
description:
Lopchu is a Darjeeling garden north-east of the town, halfway to Kalimpong and close to Sikkim, with Glenburn just over a hill. It has 226 acres under tea, and the name comes from the Lepcha language spoken there when the garden began.

Most of its plants are said to have been brought from Yunnan, which puts it on the China-type side of Darjeeling. The tea is black, made along usual regional lines.

What people remember is the smell and a smoky note, which sets it apart from the high, floral image of Darjeeling. Brew it hot and try it plain before adding anything.

Much of it is exported to Germany and elsewhere in Europe, while in India it is a long-standing brand with loyal drinkers. Buy recent packs, since aroma is the point.
history:
The garden was established in the early 1860s, under British planters who may have been the Brown family. Cousins and jute traders S.N. and G.L. Kanoria bought it in 1954, and their grandsons Rajesh and Sandeep Kanoria have since owned it.

The Economic Times has described Lopchu as a 90-year-old brand with a dedicated global following.
